title: Baking & Pastry
tagline: Breads, laminated doughs, cakes, and chocolate — the dedicated pastry path.
summary: A deep-dive specialization of the Culinary & Hospitality roadmap: the baking and pastry career from bread fundamentals through laminated doughs, cakes, chocolate, production planning, and the home-bakery business.

detail.description: Baking splits into bread (lean and enriched doughs, fermentation), pastry (laminated doughs, plated desserts, chocolate), and production (bakeries, hotels, wholesale) — precision-driven and schedule-shaped.
detail.why: Baking rewards precision and patience — it is a craft with clear skills, steady demand, and a strong self-employment path.
learn: Read the BLS OOH bakers profile
Compare bread vs pastry vs production environments
Visit a bakery at 4 a.m. to see the reality
Choose a lane to develop first
tasks: Mix and bake ingredients to produce breads, pastries, and other baked goods.

detail.description: Bread craft: lean vs enriched doughs, fermentation control, shaping, scoring, steam, and hearing crust crackle — the oldest and most fundamental baking skill.
detail.why: Bread teaches fermentation, timing, and feel — the foundation every pastry skill builds on.
learn: Bake lean hearth breads consistently for weeks
Master shaping: boules, batards, baguettes
Learn fermentation timing by temperature
Bake enriched breads (brioche, challah)

detail.description: The showpiece craft: croissants and puff pastry built by laminating butter into dough — folding, chilling, and rolling with temperature discipline.
detail.why: Lamination is the technique that proves pastry skill — every layer visible in the crumb.
learn: Make croissant dough and laminate properly
Control butter temperature throughout
Bake to shatter-crisp, honeycombed crumb
Compare butter brands and flour strengths

detail.description: Cake craft: mixing methods, leveling and filling, crumb coats, buttercream and fondant finishing, and the stacking/structure basics behind celebration cakes.
detail.why: Cakes are the highest-ticket custom work — wedding and celebration cakes fund many home businesses.
learn: Bake level, even cake layers consistently
Master buttercream texture and smoothing
Learn stacking and dowel structure safely
Practice one decorated showpiece

detail.description: Restaurant pastry: composed plated desserts with sauces, textures, and temperature contrasts — designed fast and executed to order on the line.
detail.why: Plated dessert work is the restaurant pastry chef's daily craft — creativity at service speed.
learn: Build desserts with 3+ components and one sauce
Design for execution in 5 minutes at pickup
Learn mousse, curd, and tuile components
Plate for the camera honestly

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Formulation literacy: baker's percentages (everything relative to flour), scaling accuracy, hydration effects, and adjusting formulas for batch size and environment.
detail.why: Percentages turn recipes into systems — the professional language of every bakery.
learn: Convert 5 recipes to baker's percentages
Scale formulas up and down cleanly
Adjust hydration for flour and weather
Cost one formula per serving

detail.description: Bakery production is choreography: par-bakes and retarders, overnight proofs, oven scheduling, and hitting the case-full deadline every morning.
detail.why: Production planning is what separates home bakers from professional bakers — it's the promotable skill.
learn: Plan a 200-unit morning bake on paper
Learn retarder/proof box scheduling
Build par levels from sales data
Execute one full production shift

detail.description: The showpiece arts: tempering chocolate for shine and snap, ganaches, pulled and blown sugar, and isomalt work — competition-level display skills.
detail.why: Chocolate and sugar work are pastry's high-art corner — competition and hotel showpiece careers live here.
learn: Temper chocolate properly (seed method) consistently
Make ganache for different uses
Practice basic pulled-sugar pieces
Build one small chocolate showpiece

detail.description: Baking safety: the major allergens and cross-contact control, gluten-free and vegan substitution science, and food-handler sanitation discipline.
detail.why: Allergen mistakes are medical emergencies — substitution science is now a core professional skill.
learn: Learn the major allergens and cross-contact prevention
Master one GF flour blend and its behavior
Practice vegan substitution systems
Keep sanitation certification current

detail.description: Pastry economics: ingredient costing per unit, labor time honesty, waste factors, and pricing custom work (weddings especially) to real value.
detail.why: Custom cakes and pastries underprice themselves into extinction — costing is the business survival skill.
learn: Cost 10 items per ingredient and labor hour
Learn wedding-cake pricing by servings and complexity
Build a pricing sheet you defend confidently
Track waste and adjust production

detail.description: The custom-cake business: consultations, design sketches, delivery and setup logistics, contracts with deposits, and the structural engineering of tall tiers.
detail.why: Custom cakes are the most accessible pastry business — a home kitchen, portfolio, and booking system can start it.
learn: Build a consultation-to-contract process
Learn safe stacking and transport technique
Practice a consultation conversation
Post every finished cake with story

detail.description: Most US states allow home-based sale of certain low-risk baked goods under cottage-food laws — with labeling, sales-channel, and revenue caps to learn.
detail.why: Cottage laws are the legal on-ramp for home bakeries — knowing yours prevents expensive mistakes.
learn: Read your state's cottage food law
Learn allowed foods, labels, and channels
Register or permit as required locally
Plan the commercial-kitchen upgrade path

resources.title: Forrager — cottage food laws by state

detail.description: Ladders: baker assistant → baker → head baker; pastry cook → pastry chef (hotels and restaurants); or home baker → farmers market → custom business → storefront.
detail.why: Pastry ladders reward precision plus reliability — every shift is an audition for the next rung.
learn: Map the ladder in your target setting
Choose bread, pastry, or cake depth first
Find a mentor pastry chef or baker
Build a portfolio of consistent work

detail.description: Baking runs nights and early mornings on your feet, with heat, repetition, and holiday peaks — sleep systems, body care, and honest pacing are career equipment.
detail.why: The craft's physical schedule ends more careers than skill does — planning for it is professional.
learn: Build a night-shift sleep system
Protect wrists and backs with technique
Plan holiday-peak staffing and pricing
Keep one weekday fully off, always
